Keeping peptides cool in Tempe

Tempe has its own NOAA station, TEMPE ASU, at about 1,167 feet and some 2.6 miles north-northeast of the city's Census center point.23 Its 1991 to 2020 normals give July a 105.9 °F high and a 75.8 °F low, and January a 70.6 °F high and a 38.5 °F low.2 The station averages 106.8 days a year at or above 100 °F and 179.1 at or above 90 °F, with 9.7 nights at or below freezing and 8.80 inches of precipitation a year.1

Phoenix Sky Harbor, about 5 miles to the west, has a similar July high of 106.5 °F, but its nights are far warmer: 84.5 °F in July against Tempe's 75.8 °F, and 46.0 °F in January against 38.5 °F.26 A July day in Tempe can swing about 30 °F between afternoon and night,2 and the afternoon is what a parcel on a doorstep meets.

Mixing a vial calls for care of its own. FDA labels for approved freeze-dried products describe the technique: run the diluent down the inside wall of the vial rather than onto the powder, then swirl or roll it gently instead of shaking, to avoid foaming.54 Both tesamorelin labels say to use a solution only if it is clear and colorless with no particles.57 The two labels differ on how long a mixed vial lasts, and the EGRIFTA WR label says the two formulations are not substitutable, so neither limit transfers to a research peptide.7 The storage guide covers freezer and fridge storage, and the reconstitution calculator handles the concentration math.

About Tempe

Tempe began at a river crossing. In 1871 Charles Trumbull Hayden, one of its founders, started the Hayden Ferry at the Salt River "Narrows", now the entrance to downtown, and the Mill Avenue bridge was built at the ferry crossing in 1931.8 More than a century later the dry riverbed became Tempe Town Lake. Central Arizona Project water began filling it on June 2, 1999, and it opened to the public on November 7, 1999, after a festival that drew more than 35,000 people.8

The Census Bureau estimates 190,571 residents on July 1, 2025, on 40.0 square miles of land.93 It is a young, renting city: the median age is 30.0, against 37.6 for Maricopa County, and about 57.7 percent of occupied homes are rented, against about 34.8 percent countywide (American Community Survey, 2020 to 2024).1011

Arizona State University's Tempe campus, established in 1885, is ASU's original home.12 It has 46,476 undergraduate and 8,836 graduate and professional students and 3,433 faculty, and it awarded 14,597 degrees in 2024 to 2025.12 Landmarks include Palm Walk, Old Main, the ASU Art Museum and ASU Gammage, designed by Frank Lloyd Wright.12 ASU's Biodesign Institute occupies three buildings with 540,000 square feet on the campus and houses more than 1,500 faculty, staff and students.13 Its shared facilities include the Compact X-ray Free Electron Laser Lab, the DNASU Plasmid Repository and core labs for genomics, mass spectrometry and imaging.13

Frequently asked questions

Do you ship research peptides to Tempe?

Yes. Tempe is compact, with about 40 square miles of land,3 and every address in it is served the same way: orders ship from the USA and Canada and follow the shipping policy used across the United States. Strengths, price and stock are shown on each product page before checkout. A parcel that arrives damaged, short or with the wrong item is handled through the returns page.

Why can a mixed vial look cloudy after it comes out of the fridge?

Cold can do it. The FDA label for one somatropin product, ZOMACTON, says some cloudiness may occur after refrigeration, that the product should warm to room temperature, and that it should not be used if the cloudiness persists.4 The same label warns that shaking or vigorous mixing makes the solution cloudy.4 The EGRIFTA SV (tesamorelin) label says to use a solution only if it is clear, colorless and free of particles.5 Those rules belong to approved products; for a research vial, its own label, product page and documents are the guide.

Is there a D2C Peptides location near the ASU campus?

No. D2C Peptides lists no location in Tempe, near the campus or anywhere else in the county, so no address appears here. Tempe orders are handled by shipping only. To reach us, use the contact page. All Maricopa County pages, plus a table comparing summer heat at seven NOAA stations, are on Peptides in Phoenix.

Does HCG need special supplies for lab preparation?

The HCG product page lists the supplies sold for preparing it, including bacteriostatic water, insulin syringes and alcohol swabs. The reconstitution guide describes the lab steps, and Peptide supplies explained describes what each item is for. HCG strength is given in international units, 5000 IU per vial, so concentration math starts from units rather than milligrams.
